choices.pr_choice: The law is stated for arbitrary subgroups H, K and a subgroup N that is normal in the whole group G.
choices.excerpt: prove `⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆` for `N` normal
choices.status_reason: The title and the description's first paragraph state the law for N normal.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief must state the hypothesis to state the result; the title fixes it.
choices.consequence: A weaker hypothesis would make the law usable in more situations; a stronger one in fewer.

choices.pr_choice: The law is an equality of subgroups with the join in the first commutator argument, the commutator of the join on the left side and the join of commutators on the right.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_left (H K N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ := by
choices.status_reason: The title and the description's first paragraph state exactly this equation.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states the equation as the title gives it; the task cannot be given without it.
choices.consequence: The orientation sets the rewriting direction (distributing versus collecting) for users and automation.

choices.pr_choice: All three subgroups are explicit binders in the order H, K, N, and normality of N is an instance argument.
choices.consequence: Implicit subgroups, another order, or normality as an explicit hypothesis change how callers apply and rewrite with the law.

choices.pr_choice: The two laws are named commutator_sup_left and commutator_sup_right, the suffix naming the commutator argument that holds the join.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_right (N H K : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅N, H ⊔ K⁆ = ⁅N, H⁆ ⊔ ⁅N, K⁆ := by
choices.consequence: Names are how users find the result; another scheme (for example sup_commutator or commutator_sup_distrib) changes discoverability.

choices.pr_choice: The PR also adds the companion law with the join in the second argument, [N, H ⊔ K] = [N, H] ⊔ [N, K].
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_right (N H K : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅N, H ⊔ K⁆ = ⁅N, H⁆ ⊔ ⁅N, K⁆ := by
choices.consequence: Without it users must commute the arguments themselves; with it there is one more declaration to maintain.

choices.pr_choice: The companion takes its subgroups in the order N, H, K, with the normal subgroup first, unlike the first law's H, K, N.
choices.consequence: The explicit-argument order differs between the two laws, which affects callers who supply the subgroups positionally.

choices.pr_choice: The two laws are multiplicative only: they carry no to_additive, although the helper lemmas added beside them do.
choices.consequence: Users of additive subgroups get no distributive law; adding to_additive would provide it.

choices.pr_choice: The laws carry no simp or other attribute.
choices.consequence: Tagging them simp would make the simplifier distribute commutators over joins, which may or may not be the wanted normal form.

choices.pr_choice: The two laws have no docstrings.
choices.excerpt: +theorem commutator_sup_left (H K N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ := by
choices.consequence: A docstring would make the result visible in the documentation as a named law.

choices.pr_choice: The proof restricts to M = H ⊔ K ⊔ N, shows [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] is normal in M by bounding the normalizer, and computes in the quotient by [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] through a private auxiliary.
choices.consequence: The route is what calls for the helper lemmas and for the move of the normalizer lemma into a file the commutator file imports; another route might need neither.

choices.pr_choice: The companion is derived from the first law by symmetry of the commutator.
A private auxiliary, named with a prime, proves the same equation under the hypothesis that [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] is normal instead of N.
choices.excerpt: private theorem commutator_sup_left' (H K N : Subgroup G) [(⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆).Normal] :
choices.consequence: Kept private, the version under a different hypothesis is unavailable to users; public, it would be a further result to name and maintain.

choices.pr_choice: The PR adds three public helpers: monotonicity of the commutator in each argument separately, and [K₁, K₂] ≤ K when K₁ ≤ K and K₂ ≤ K.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_mono_left (h : H₁ ≤ H₂) : ⁅H₁, K⁆ ≤ ⁅H₂, K⁆ :=
choices.consequence: Three new public declarations; they could instead be inlined through the existing two-sided monotonicity lemma or kept private.

choices.pr_choice: The helpers are named commutator_mono_left, commutator_mono_right and commutator_le_of_le.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_mono_right (h : K₁ ≤ K₂) : ⁅H, K₁⁆ ≤ ⁅H, K₂⁆ :=
choices.consequence: Public names fix how users find these facts.

choices.pr_choice: The one-sided monotonicity helpers are tagged to_additive with the gcongr attribute; commutator_le_of_le gets to_additive only.
choices.consequence: gcongr registration makes the helpers available to congruence automation (the PR's own proof rewrites with grw); without it that automation does not see them.

choices.pr_choice: The helpers do not bind their subgroups in the signature; they take them from the file's section variables and state only the order hypotheses as arguments, unlike the laws, which bind their subgroups explicitly.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_le_of_le (h₁ : K₁ ≤ K) (h₂ : K₂ ≤ K) : ⁅K₁, K₂⁆ ≤ K :=
choices.consequence: Whether the subgroups are explicit decides whether callers can name them positionally or use dot notation.

choices.pr_choice: The laws, the auxiliary and the helpers all go into the existing commutator file.
The one-sided monotonicity helpers sit right after commutator_mono, the bound right after commutator_le_sup, and the laws after `variable (H₁ H₂)` before commutator_characteristic.
The PR moves and renames the existing normalizer lemma as part of this contribution.

choices.status_reason: The description's third paragraph states the move and the rename.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states that the lemma moves to an earlier file and is renamed for consistent naming, without the target or the new name.
choices.consequence: Leaving it in place would keep it out of reach of files that cannot import Pointwise.lean; the rename changes what users type.

choices.pr_choice: The lemma moves from Subgroup/Pointwise.lean into the existing Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean.
choices.visibility_reason: packet: base files; the description also says an earlier file.
choices.consequence: The file decides which other files can use the lemma without a heavier import.

choices.pr_choice: The moved lemma and its aliases sit after le_normalizer_of_normal and immediately before inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_inf.
The new name is inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_sup (and its additive translation), patterned on the neighbouring inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_inf.
choices.status_reason: The description's third paragraph says the rename matches inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_inf, which nearly fixes the name.
choices.visibility_reason: Partly: the brief passes on that the rename is for consistency with related names but gives neither the sibling nor the new name; with the base file a designer can derive it.
choices.consequence: The name is what every caller types; a different pattern would not match the sibling.

choices.pr_choice: The moved lemma keeps its statement, proof and to_additive verbatim, including the explicit (H K : Subgroup G) binders and the normalizer of the coerced set, while its sibling inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_inf takes H and K from section variables.
choices.excerpt:
lemma inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_sup (H K : Subgroup G) :
    normalizer H ⊓ normalizer K ≤ normalizer ((H ⊔ K : Subgroup G) : Set G) := by
choices.consequence: Restating it to match the sibling's binders would break callers that pass H and K positionally or use dot notation.

choices.pr_choice: The old multiplicative and additive names stay usable after the rename instead of being removed.
choices.status_reason: Follows from the rename under Mathlib's practice of not breaking downstream names without notice.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief says code using the current names must still resolve; the mechanism is not given.
choices.consequence: Removing the old names would break downstream code at once.

choices.consequence: It makes the pointwise subgroup file depend on commutator theory, changing the import graph and what rebuilds; without it some downstream file may lose a transitive import.

choices.pr_choice: The indexed sibling of the moved lemma stays in Pointwise.lean under its current name; only the binary version moves.

choices.pr_choice: Only the binary join is treated; no law for the join of an indexed family of subgroups is added.

choices.pr_choice: The inclusion [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] ≤ [H ⊔ K, N], which needs no normality, is proved only inside a proof and not stated as its own lemma.

feasibility_reason: The brief states the law at the generality the title fixes (H, K arbitrary, N normal in G) and the move and rename of the existing normalizer lemma that the description's third paragraph reports, with the callers and the old names that must keep working. The exposed choices are the ones the task cannot be stated without: the equation and its hypothesis (c1, c2, from the title), the fact of the move and rename (c19), and old names staying usable (c24). The new name of the moved lemma (c22) is partly exposed: the brief passes on that the rename is for consistent naming, which with the base file lets a designer derive it; the description makes that name nearly forced. File placements (c17, c20) show through the base files. Every other consequential proposed choice stays hidden: the names and binders of the laws, the companion law, the helpers and their gcongr registration, the private auxiliary, the proof route, the missing to_additive, the deprecation mechanism and the import added to Pointwise.lean.
brief_omits: The description's second paragraph (the proof idea, computing in a quotient) is withheld as a proof route, and the brief says nothing about the subgroup that proof divides by. The name of the sibling lemma the rename matches is not given, to keep the new name from being stated. The helper lemmas, the private auxiliary, the import added to Pointwise.lean and the indexed sibling lemma left in place are design choices and are not mentioned. The question whether the normality-free inclusion should be its own lemma is left out because the inputs never raise it. Open questions about the companion law, the additive form and indexed joins are posed neutrally, mixing one the PR took (the companion) with ones it did not.
